notes.title: Multiplayer | Devlog #4
notes.notes:
[h1] 🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Hey there Escapists!

Last week we had a [u][url="https://steamcommunity.com/games/3296060/announcements/detail/538864124750202555"]blog on multiplayer systems[/url][/u] - the super cool stuff that’ll help you get along with your teammate a little better - outlines, pings, and emotes! However, we wanted to dedicate a blog to go over the concept of multiplayer as a whole, how it’s shaping up for [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/url][/u], and some of what you can expect.[/p][h1]Not enough time to read?[/h1][p align="start"]That’s okay. Luckily for you, we’ve got that handled. Check out our YouTube devlog on multiplayer![/p][p align="start"][/p][previewyoutube="vcKvOSfG8Ww;full"][/previewyoutube][h1]Why Good Multiplayer is Important[/h1][p align="start"]Escape Academy 1’s multiplayer was exactly what you’d expect out of a co-op escape room experience: you could give your partner items, and they existed in the same space as you while you solved puzzles. This did its job well, as you wouldn’t be exploring larger areas, but during some playtests for Escape Academy 2, we realized that multiplayer needed some upgrades.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h1]Our Process[/h1][p align="start"][u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy 1[/url][/u] taught us that playtesting is incredibly important. Just look at these internal documents I “borrowed” from our [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/6609cfbd85bb33d94f7fa05b1ce45de7cb5ac6cd.png"][/img]retrospective last year![/p][p][/p][p align="start"]While we were playtesting, we found a couple of issues with multiplayer that made it a little difficult for players to get the full experience out of an open-world game. But, we were missing something.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/9482a433b523336a0bee0775d719d6d330c4c271.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url][/u], our pool of playtesters is [i]much[/i] larger and we’re making sure to use this to our advantage. With the first game, we let it fall behind for the reasons listed above, and this led to some of our puzzles in the later portions of the game losing the consistency we built with the early portions of the game. You might not have even noticed this as a player, but to us as a studio, it was leagues of difference.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/bcdb6be3cd22ab3f87e4236d982ad1eac151187f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Consistent playtesting has led us to be a lot happier, and much more confident, when it comes to our puzzle/world design with [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url][/u]. Now, whenever we’re making something, we try not to call it fun until we’ve seen another player have fun with it. And even then, we want to playtest it over and over again to make sure that what we’re seeing is genuine enjoyment out of puzzle lovers like us.[/p][p align="start"]Playtesting has been a huge help for building out our open-world multiplayer.[/p][p][/p][h1][i]Open-World[/i] Multiplayer[/h1][p align="start"]A large campus brings large demands. Meet Player 1 and Player 2 - two of our playtesters here to help demonstrate how we came to the addition of the new multiplayer systems we introduced in our last blog.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f6887c1eadbadfd177a2c6b27d2dbbb99f01b58f.png"][/img][/p][p]Nice to meet you, Player 1 and Player 2! Let’s take a look at how your playtests went.[/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 1:[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/27b03cd1bb0e984d9f650047d644c847c11cd7e5.png"][/img][/p][p]Player 1 is not the best when it comes to descriptive language - but Player 2 has the projector still that leads to one of the 3 answers needed for this puzzle. So, Player 1 says:

”I think you can put that projector still in that projector over there”

But Player 2 is beyond lost. “Over where? I don’t see it!” Well, it’s certainly not on the ceiling.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Thanks to Player 2, Escape Academy now has pings for the first time ever.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/146b563d6670a74617676ebd8e7447eedd7110c4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 2:[/h1][p align="start"]Both players just finished an escape room. Great! But now they’re just standing there. Menacingly. Soullessly.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/18d1ca2755b9f761b992dc43062c15a40c05a229.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]However, our brand-new WIP emotes system is bound to fix that and give Player 1 and Player 2 an outlet to let out some of that extra energy. Let’s celebrate![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/1600e50c74e5a8ebf945326d8e9fa4190749aa9c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Challenge 3:[/h1][p align="start"]Lastly, it’s easy to get lost in an open world campus. You might be able to meet up in a designated spot on campus, or just learn the map, but to us, being able to keep a close eye on your partner makes staying together a little bit easier.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Now, no matter where you are, you can keep a close eye on your partner. Whether they know it or not.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/b67c6cc8e543250bc31c2bb00b9f6a4f177973e0.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h1]My Fun Is Not Your Fun[/h1][p align="start"]Lastly, one of the biggest lessons we learned while making multiplayer, and subsequently playtesting the multiplayer experience, is that fun is subjective. I won’t go too deep into this here because it’s quite the lengthy topic and this blog is already quite tall, but if you want to see a talk on this, [u][url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGpFEv1-mAo"]Gabe Newell has an excellent interview with a behavioural psychologist where he talks all about it.[/url][/u][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Regardless, playtesting has taught us a lot about what “fun” is, and as compared to Escape Academy 1, we’ve made a vow to ourselves to not call something fun until we’ve seen someone else have fun with it first.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h1]See you next time![/h1][p align="start"]Hopefully you’re excited for multiplayer too - but what you see here isn’t the end of the road for us. We want your suggestions! If you have anything on your “Escape Academy 2’s Multiplayer Wishlist”, please let us know in the comments and we’ll take a deeper look at it![/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]If you’re excited about multiplayer too, make sure to let us know by [b][i][u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]putting us on your wishlist[/url][/u][/i][/b]. And if you made it here, thank you for reading.

With love,[/p][p align="start"]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p][p][/p][h1] 🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1][p][/p]

notes.title: Multiplayer Systems | Devlog #3
notes.notes: [h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2: BACK 2 SCHOOL!🔔[/url][/h1][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Hey Escapists![/p][p align="start"]We hope you enjoyed our [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YumDGaGDJGg&ab_channel=CoinCrewGames"]first longform devlog on YouTube[/url]; expect another one soon! 👀[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]One of our favourite staples of Escape Academy 1 was the multiplayer interactions that led to silly moments, or gave way to fun conversations with players. Bringing people together is fun! [url="https://www.coincrew.games/"]I mean, it’s even in our motto[/url].[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]So far, we’ve had a few questions on the topic of multiplayer interactions:[/p][list][*][p]Will there be online multiplayer?[/p][/*][*][p]Splitscreen couch co-op? 🥺[/p][/*][*][p]Toggleable splitscreen?[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]To put the answers shortly:[/p][h1]YES! [i]and…[/i][/h1][p align="start"]There’s also a couple of things we’re adding to change up the way duos will explore the Academy - both to help with interacting in an open world, and to make the multiplayer experience that much more interesting.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Let’s take a look 🧐[/p][h1]What’s Different?[/h1][p align="start"]It’s a bird! It’s a plane! It’s a….[b][i]ping?[/i][/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/10bbfe2124dadbfc402bcc6b601ae11263729f62.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to an escape room, things are a lot more localized. You can say “Hey, come check this out!” and walk a few feet over to your partner. Maybe your duo will point out something “[b][i]over there, by that desk.[/i][/b]” But when you’re exploring a giant sprawling campus, “over there” becomes a bit….confusing. Pings have quickly become a staple in many multiplayer experiences, and we think that bringing them into the world of Escape Academy will help make solving puzzles together less frustrating, while also leading to some silly interactions.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/2277986f943d23d8e3bc2feafe1aded0f510a72d.png"][/img][/p][h1]What if I get lost?[/h1][p align="start"]That’s a fair argument. If you’ve been keeping up with our devlogs and short-form content, it’s a very real concern. Escape Academy is the leading academy in the art of Escape, after all![/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]While many multiplayer games might opt to leash you within a certain range of the first player, we don’t want players to be limited to any single area - that can take away from the open world experience. So instead, cutting-edge Academy technology will allow you to see where your partner is on campus at any given point![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f71fe89423515b2fbf8edb773b96809801473d7c.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Still struggling to find eachother?[/b] That’s okay. The gazebo in the middle of campus is an excellent place to relax and meet up before planning your next escape.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/90ceb385a4b7115ce3b6e13a8bf22dd1c9de2d48.png"][/img][/p][h1]Emotes🥳💃[/h1][p]Every good Escapist needs a way to express themselves. We’re bringing emotes to Escape Academy as a way to help players communicate, for the better or for the worse. Solved that difficult puzzle? That deserves a thumbs up! Struggling with a spinner lock? Seems like the perfect opportunity for a sarcastic clap.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/ed3695796825988e3676e595c7bfce20974f8a66.png"][/img][/p][h1]What else?[/h1][p align="start"]One of the complaints from playtesters we’ve gotten is that splitscreen modes in online gameplay can be a little disorienting. So, just like in Escape Academy 1, you’ll have the option to switch between the splitscreen and widescreen views if motion sickness is something that affects you.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/e6611761ece3f3be32b5c5e42ebbae53e6ab780b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Partner taking a little too long to unpause in couch co-op? Time to take things into your own hands.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/7546d425b6969614d093ba02846d9fb09957fe29.png"][/img][/p][p]Lastly, to keep things from being a little too janky (or asking for a little too much out of your computer), players will have to enter escape rooms together. Always remember that two minds are better than one! Usually.[/p][p][/p][h1]See you in the next one![/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/94d7eaff66b82734043c6f5dd335d683e9eedde6.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re hoping multiplayer features will give [i]just[/i] the right amount of sass to multiplayer interactions, and help to immerse you in the world of Escape Academy a little bit. If you have anything on your wishlist for Escape Academy 2 features, just let us know in the comments![/p][p][/p][p]That’s all from us - [i]for now. [/i]Stay tuned for another longform devlog coming soon, and don’t forget to…[/p][h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2: BACK 2 SCHOOL!🔔[/url][/h1][p][/p][p]With Love,[/p][p align="start"]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p]

notes.title: How Did We Get Here? | Devlog #2
notes.notes:
[p]Welcome back, Escapists![/p][p] [/p][p]We’re here again this week with another devlog, this time digging deeper at some stuff from behind the scenes - despite some sneak peeks at our quests system here and some short-form content there, you might catch yourself wondering:[/p][h1]How Did We Get Here?[/h1][p]Let’s go back. Waaaay back. Our studio, [url="https://www.coincrew.games/"]Coin Crew Games[/url], was founded in 2018 with one simple goal in mind: to bring people together through play. It started with arcade cabinets, and over time as we grew as a team, we started to branch out with some other goals in mind. With the ongoing pandemic in 2020, we were led to [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url]’s conception - our first full-fledged puzzle video game that could be played by anyone, anywhere, in your own home.[/p][p] [/p][p]Staring at the Steam store, our [b]co-founder Wyatt[/b] recounts: “[i]…We didn't see any local co-op escape room games on the store pages. As a team, we love local co-op games like Towerfall, Speedrunners, and Overcooked are all games that we really enjoy playing, so there not being a solid escape room version felt like a gap in the market.[/i]” It was a daunting project, and the co-op elements meant you could play with your friends and family from a distance. Given that arcade games were supposed to last a few minutes before being replayed, which was challenging enough to make, a gameplay experience for [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url] that would last 4-6 hours was an exciting [b][i]and[/i][/b] intimidating task.[/p][p] [/p][p]Over the next couple years, we would put thousands of hours into the creation of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/"]Escape Academy[/url]. After mountains of effort and learning, we could finally put down our pencils and say that it was finished. However, at this point it was time to take our vision a step further.[/p][h1]Starting A Sequel[/h1][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/url] has been in development for nearly a year now. In that time we’ve been using all the lessons that Escape Academy 1 gave us - one of the most important of those lessons being that we made [i]just about[/i] every mistake you can make in the design of our original game engine.[/p][p] [/p][p]Given our ambitions going into the sequel, and wanting to avoid inheriting the bugs from the first engine, we had to make a difficult decision. That’s why before we could even get started with 2, it was time to burn down the first engine and start completely over. So, we were here:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/14c30a127962989c27f3d6056c4c1814e3f4cda1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]It was a blessing [b]and[/b] a curse, in many different ways. Starting over meant, well, [i]starting from nothing[/i]. But starting over [b]also[/b] meant we could use those lessons we learned from the [i]first[/i] game to build bigger and even better.[/p][p] [/p][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url] started as two pictures:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/f7ff91f0eb579d746077eac51aa89819eb13c683.png"][/img][/p][p]It would be an open world experience where you could talk to NPCs and be taken through quests and puzzle rooms while exploring a whimsical academy that teaches the art of escape. It evolved to a collection of questions, that went something like this:[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p][i]How do we make a sequel?[/i][/p][list][*][p]We know that we don’t want Escape Academy 1.5. We want [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]Escape Academy 2[/url]. A sequel shouldn’t feel like a bunch of extra level packs, but rather be a completely transformative take on the world of Escape Academy.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][i]Is this possible?[/i][/p][list][*][p]There’s [b]open-world games[/b], and there’s [b]escape room games[/b]. But this time, we’re doing [b]both[/b] - how does one accomplish that?[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][i]How do open-world mechanics change a puzzle game?[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]How can we learn from the mistakes we made in the past?[/i][/p][/*][/list][p][i]Don’t let these questions fool you[/i] - [i]every[/i] answer would have a [b]counterargument[/b], and every point has its own [b]counterpoint[/b]. Plenty of ideas would be thrown around, some kept, some scrapped, and we watched as the world of Escape Academy itself evolved with our ideas.[/p][p] [/p][p]Now, it was time to begin [i]prototyping[/i].[/p][h1]The Prototype[/h1][p]The first (and completely, totally sane) version of our game looked something like this:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/300e22eb9d8c1b9718981d012ffeb564e98d8b8c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We had this idea for a first escape room where you have to escape from detention, and so we assembled a super basic test environment that allowed us to see what that might be like. We were pretty much trying to get an idea of how our new engine was working, because in these early stages there’s always bugs and problems you need to look out for. In these polished devlogs, you don’t always get to see the trials and tribulations that game development really can be - but trust me - the team has had our fair share of late night troubleshooting, even back then.[/p][p] [/p][p]This also happened to be the point in our development process where we introduced the quests system - If you’ve read our last blog post ([url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3296060/view/538860320326680900?l=english"]which you definitely should, by the way[/url]) you’ll notice it looks a lot different here![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/74ee2d04eab2f77a63886e1dc94359775a9a3e70.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h1]Building The Campus[/h1][p]Now that we’d nailed down a prototype and had our game engine in a spot we were happy with, we could start thinking about what an open-world escape room experience would truly look like.[/p][p] [/p][p]3 weeks of combined engineering, design, narrative, and art efforts led us here! This is one of the earliest stages of the campus you’ll see, and this foundation was a glorious first step.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/fd721e1459bbaf3781fd0a86f86da911f7eeb40f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Past this point, we started to think of the first areas that could be interesting to design escape rooms in, especially now that we could start visualizing how quests would function - maybe you run from that tower overlooking everything to the dome over on the right. We set our sights on Humanities - the section of the Academy where you’d learn about the history and culture of Escape.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/fa89d5f6b12532593dcdd458d043b737a1c8f53f.png"][/img][/p][p]This area was incredibly impactful to the team, because we were finally getting into the big chunks of open-world gameplay that players would experience. We designed our first big puzzles for Escape Academy 2 here, and if you’ve seen our [url="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/B-xvxIkxyts"]viral Aztec Lock video[/url], this area will end up being very familiar👀
[/p][p]The Humanities area also marked the point where research began to play a major part in our process. When designing puzzles, we would often find ourselves miles-deep in research rabbitholes trying to find interesting ways to tie puzzles in to other cultures, and fun ways to tie the Escape Academy lore/history into our puzzles as well. It was a very educational process for the entire team, especially because we were getting back into the swing of things with game development after Escape Academy. Humanities got to stretch beyond just a campus area - it became a massive milestone marker of what our hard work had become![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/d9b8c134582b9be1070e377a64ad8f51de2a4f3f.gif"][/img][/p][p]                                  I don’t think I remember Escape Bucks looking like that…[/p][p][/p][p]At this time in our development process, we began to swap between escape room design and open-world design because often times, an escape room would demand something from our open-world environment or vice versa. Sometimes we’d go back and change things because narrative would change, or maybe something wouldn’t play how we wanted. Months and months of work later, our process would lead us here: we created the Headmaster’s Tower as you know it, in all its glory![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/7e5b3e4f062ad4df7a2e8c2802dd070913726ee6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Don’t be fooled![/h1][p]Don’t let these quick snapshots into our development process make you think it was easy - game design is hard, and what you’re seeing is nearly a [i]year[/i] of combined efforts from a team of around ten people. We’re incredibly grateful for those of you who have been following us, because keeping this exciting project secret for almost a year was not easy.[/p][p] [/p][p]Next week, we plan to dive a little deeper into all of this on our [url="https://www.youtube.com/@coincrewgames/featured"]YouTube channel[/url] and really give you a thorough look at what the timeline up to Humanities was like for us - but we hope this teaser has satiated your curiosity for now😉[/p][p] [/p][p]What are you dying to know in the development process? When it comes to these devlogs, what speaks most to you? Let us know in the comments![/p][p]And as always, don’t forget to:[/p][h1][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]🔔WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2🔔[/url][/h1][p]and we’ll see you in the next one.[/p][p] [/p][p]With Love,[/p][p]Coin Crew Games💛💜[/p]

notes.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School Devlog #1 - Quests!
notes.notes: [p][i]Dear Escapists[/i],[/p][p]You read that right. Welcome to our first devlog; a series where we’ll be taking a dive into some of the things we’re dreaming up for [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"][i]Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School[/i][/url]. Our work-in-progress quest system is the first system (of many!) we’re excited to show you.[/p][p][/p][h1]Why Quests?[/h1][p]From a top-down perspective, [b]critical quests[/b] and escape rooms advance you through the story and important narrative events, while [b]side quests[/b] allow for a natural way to interact with the campus environment and other students. That’s not to say side quests won’t reward you for your hard work, though![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/43cd6217a67f0b2c1dfc725e6cfd72873f48ce00.png"][/img][/p][p]When it comes to quests, there are two types: critical path and side quests, and it’s taken a lot of trial-and-error to reach that point.[/p][p]We want the side quests to be obvious enough that you don’t miss them, secret enough that you feel rewarded when you encounter them, and clear enough that you don’t end up doing a side quest on accident when you want to progress the story. So, we’ve found ourselves tweaking things as small as wording in text, lighting, etc. to draw the player’s attention in [i]just the right way[/i] without being too obvious or intrusive.[/p][p]                [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/05b33fcb833d4fe83334769f02f8dec283b63920.png"][/img][/p][p]               These are just a few of the quest-givers you’ll find throughout the Academy…🔒[/p][p]                                Blue Icon = Critical Path | Red Icon = Extra Credit! 🔥[/p][p][/p][p]One of my personal favorite things about quests is that they let the entire world be littered with puzzles instead of rooms, which in my opinion gives so much more life and personality to the campus. Here are some of the questions you might have about the upcoming quests system (feel free to drop your own in the comments!):[/p][p] [/p][h1]What makes quests meaningful?[/h1][p]Currently, we have quests that progress the main story, and some quests that are optional. (In our demo build, you can go on a quest to bring food to the cat in your dorm, and have a furry friend that follows you around!)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/e4f71c11b2fa0a2a214825b0b2b052fe7c844610.png"][/img]              Maybe having a cat isn't [i]required[/i], but it's definitely a gameplay-enhancer on all fronts.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/a760dc56ae585206a96103c0d3691e8bdda3ffe7.png"][/img][/p][p]Unlike Escape Academy 1, [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"][i]Escape Academy 2[/i][/url][i] [/i]will have a fully-fleshed out campus that you can explore to your heart’s content. One of the benefits of an open-world campus is that there’s many more opportunities for narrative.[/p][p]That’s one of the biggest reasons we chose to implement this[i] [/i]system, and we know you’ll love to explore the world at your own pace while uncovering the secrets of Escape Academy in a rewarding, fully-immersive environment. Quests help so much with this effort, because you end up with a nudge forward, without feeling like you’re solving puzzles “just because”.[/p][p] [/p][p]For quests that don’t directly contribute to the main story, we still want quests to be rewarding and meaningful, which is why a lot of these side quests will be tied to a system called…[/p][h1]Escape Bucks![/h1][p]Escape Bucks are a currency (don’t worry, no microtransactions here) that enables you to travel around campus in various ways. Maybe you spend 3 Escape Bucks to bribe the librarian, or drop 1 Escape Buck into the vending machine for a can of ESCAPIST’S EDGE![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/0671e5b0cf670f440c1fd04a4a2bacd74744fa3e.png"][/img][/p][p]From a game-design perspective, we love the Escape Bucks system, because it introduces a fictional currency that makes side quests feel more rewarding. Sometimes during the main story you’ll need to buy items (such as books or school supplies) to advance, and Escape Bucks are the perfect system for that. This also ensures side quests become a more important part of the game, because we don’t care where the money comes from but we [i]can [/i]require that you engage with [i]some[/i] of the optional content, which gives the player a little more agency and further immersion at the Academy.[/p][p]                 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/d46648ba561aaca753899c163e32b07b378e3509.png"][/img][/p][p]Lastly, Escape Bucks can also be found in hidden nooks and crannies around the campus. So don’t be afraid to talk with every NPC and look underneath every stone, locker and toilet stall - just don’t go digging in other people’s pockets. That’s rude.[/p][p][/p][h1]What were some of the challenges with implementing quests?[/h1][p]It’s required a different look at the game design. Escape rooms want you to solve [i]everything[/i] very quickly, because it’s absolutely not fun to lose just because you went down a 10-minute rabbit hole exploring what would end up being a red herring.[/p][p]Quests, on the other hand, will allow a bit more freedom in the experience. This freedom can be a blessing and a curse - it’s definitely easier to design an escape room with some story inbetween, but quests require you to think out of the box in a way that might otherwise be limited with a linear room, and that’s just one of the many reasons we’re excited to continue fleshing out the quests system.[/p][p][/p][h1]What Do You Think?[/h1][p]We’re SUPER excited about this system because it fundamentally changes how you escape and lets the player deepen the bond they’ll feel with the Academy itself while playing.[/p][p] [/p][p]However, we want to hear your thoughts too! When it comes to quests, what are your expectations? Is there anything more you want to know? Drop your answers below, and don’t forget to…[/p][h1]     🔔[url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3296060/Escape_Academy_2_Back_2_School/"]WISHLIST ESCAPE ACADEMY 2[/url]🔔[/h1][p] [/p][p]With love,[/p][p]Coin Crew Games 💛💜[/p]

notes.title: Tournament of Puzzles Steam Public Playtest Live Now!
notes.notes:
Hello Escapists,

We're back with another Steam Public Playtest of our free update, [i]Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles![/i] Take a look to see how you can get involved. 

[h1]What’s in store at the Tournament of Puzzles?[/h1]

[i]Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles[/i], takes the Academy’s students on the road with Coach Yoach to showdown at various arenas across the globe and compete for glory in multiple Escape events.

The playtest this weekend will take place at the Egyptian themed arena, The Tomb of the First Escapist, and feature three PvP modes, two of which are brand new to the Tournament of Puzzles!

[b]Escape Race: [/b]First player to solve all the puzzles, unlock all the doors, and grab the trophy wins!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/b34965a6aa17e15eb395f6dac7282d41a0cee9a9.png[/img]

[b]Tic-Tac-Toe:[/b] Solve puzzles in order to unlock your team color gems, then place them on a 3x3 tic-tac-toe grid. First to connect three wins the match!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/91e7c452fa98855114459968ab9dddf6c82442a3.png[/img]

[b]Scavenger Hunt:[/b] Throughout the level, trophies have been hidden in plain sight. First player to collect the majority of the trophies will claim victory!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/ebe4e8d71453df00c0aa4f1bde196ad1fd0b1675.png[/img]

And if you wanna take the update for a whirl but don’t have a buddy (or just want to play in sweet, sweet solitude) then check out the practice-race mode available for solo play! 

For more information on the power-ups and to-be-released arenas, strike up a conversation with Coach Yoach in the lobby. He’ll give you the lowdown on everything you can expect to find in the full update!

[h2]How do I access the Tournament of Puzzles?[/h2]

Installing the playtest build is as simple as stopping by our store page and pressing the green “request access” button under the playtest header. It will install a separate build of the game that just includes the update and will playable for a limited time only. Launch this from your Steam library and you’re on your way to puzzling!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/450aed74e5ab3a1115b37c65de31e2ea6bdff035.png[/img]

Once in the build, play through the very first level (if you haven’t already) in order to gain access to the main campus map screen. Once here, press tab to bring up the “Level Packs” screen and select the [i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i].

Now you will be in the [i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i] lobby where clicking the trophy cabinet will allow you to choose your game mode and arena track. Each mode offers a new way to engage with the puzzles and your opponent while track selection will effect your route through the massive arenas.

[i]NOTE: For now, the only arena available will be The Tomb of the First Escapist. The full update will contain two other full levels, The Hackannery, and The Showman’s Studio. This playtest does however feature all the modes that will be available in the full update, so give them all a try![/i]

For those ace Escapists who would like to go that extra mile, please fill out this [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdVguAqhkOlZA9et_HWNPlfruW16O94bHSi8H9RO2XJtBzeHw/viewform?usp=sf_link]brief Google survey[/url] so the dev team can continue to improve the experience. 

If you encounter any bugs, please feel free to drop by our [url=https://discord.gg/YMFYxeSB]Discord[/url] and visit the #🐛-buglogs channel so we can track the issues on our end and get to work on a fix.

[h2]Thanks for Playtesting[/h2]

And don’t forget to have fun out there on the Puzzle Pitch with your fellow Escapists! We’re pumped about bringing you guys in to our development process and can’t wait to hear what you have to say. 

As always--

GLHF,

Coin Crew Games

notes.title: Escape Academy - Release Schedule Update
notes.notes:
Hello Escapists!

Coin Crew Games has been hard at work testing [i]The Tournament of Puzzles[/i] update and putting the finishing touches on  our second DLC, [i]Escape Academy: Escape from the Past[/i]. We wanted to take a moment to share some updates with everyone!

[h2]Updated Release Timing for [i]The Tournament of Puzzles[/i][/h2]

First off we wanted to thank everyone who partook in our Steam Playtest of [i]The Tournament of Puzzles[/i] earlier this year. The feedback was immensely insightful and we were thrilled with the results and everyone’s thoughts. After ingesting feedback from the Steam Playtest, we made the decision to re-center the experience on PvP play. The dev team is in the process of building out new mechanics that lean into player on player interactions and maximize the frantic nature of trying to solve puzzles faster than your opponent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/5d105f28d094ae8934552c6a8ca549bbbd2b0492.png[/img]

As a result, [i]The Tournament of Puzzles[/i] is going to be coming out later than we’d originally hoped. We are now targeting a Q4 2023 release across all platforms. But there IS good news as well, which is that we’re going to be running more tests in order to build an experience that we’re all happy with! We want your involvement to yield an update we’re all proud of and one that you’ll have a hard time putting down. Keep your eyes peeled for more Steam Playtests and take a look at this [url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/escape-academy-tournament-of-puzzles-preview-gdc/]Digital Trends article[/url] to gain some more insight into our new design direction.

[h2]Learnings from the [i]Escape from Anti-Escape Island[/i] Release[/h2]

We’d also like to take a moment to share our biggest learning  from releasing our first DLC last fall: [i]Escape from Anti-Escape Island[/i] released in a buggier state than we were happy with, and you all rightfully gave us that feedback. For [i]Escape from the Past[/i], we’ve spent extra polish and QA time to make for as smooth and frustration free of an experience as possible. This is also a part of the reason we’ve decided to give [i]The Tournament of Puzzles[/i] more time in the oven. Not only do we want the design to wow everyone and fuel all sorts of puzzle rivalries, we want it to be a smooth, bug free experience.

Speaking of our upcoming DLC…

[h2]Introducing [i]Escape Academy: Escape from the Past![/i][/h2]

For those of you who caught the Nintendo Indie World stream this morning and watched our full [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eSv6XyXSeRk]Nintendo Switch, Complete Edition, Trailer[/url] you may have noticed some brand new footage from our upcoming DLC, [i]Escape Academy: Escape from the Past[/i]. This DLC is included in the Season Pass and will be released late Spring 2023!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/1c3dde07eab3d55cf6a3c8028e081a0127e03350.png[/img]

[i]Escape from the Past[/i], is a prequel that puts players in control of familiar faces Sandra Solange and Eel Barnes as they begin their journey from Academy students to the unstoppable team of master Escapists we meet in [i]Escape Academy[/i].

After an “accident” at an Academy sporting event, Headmaster Horatio Windsor believes that SOMEONE at the school wants him dead. He enlists Sandra and Eel to go undercover in order to investigate each of the suspected faculty members. As the "accidents" keep piling up, players must successfully navigate (and survive!) five, all new rooms while piecing together clues spread across each in order to deduce who the killer is. It's an Escape Academy whodunnit!

notes.title: Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles Steam Playtest is live NOW!
notes.notes:
Hello and Happy New Year fellow Escapists! 

Coin Crew Games has exciting news about our free major update: it’s titled [i]Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles[/i], it features procedurally generated escape rooms, and the best part? You can playtest it NOW using the Steam Playtest feature!

[h2]What is Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles?[/h2]

[i]Escape Academy: Tournament of Puzzles[/i] is our free, major content update which introduces one of the community's most requested features: replayable levels! 

Join Coach Yoach and his crack team of Puzzletes as they compete against other Escape schools  to bring the championship cup back home to Escape Academy!

[i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i] features procedurally generated escape rooms that take place in all new, massive arenas themed around each Escape school. Puzzle your way through the rainy, neon labyrinth at Hackademy’s “Phish Market” and do your best to survive the perils of History High’s “The Tomb of the First Escapist.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/ab1b3f0c5bc4d8ba8fe3a07ae94299ef03558d54.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/0d2f904820019aba2af834ee80bdc29fc60dba02.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/c69ba04272765124ab183ae65e31dc25a40d66db.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/d5931c6695186c9a15e54de0c7f74d593d97d084.png[/img]

Every time you compete in a heat of the tournament, you’ll encounter different puzzles and challenges, procedurally selected from our ever-growing depot of brain twisters. No two runs will be the same!

The [i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i] Playtest can be played single player or in co-op!

[b]A NOTE ABOUT MULTIPLAYER:[/b] While online play is accessible in this build, there are known desync issues that will make the completion of levels nearly impossible. We strongly urge players to stick to playing locally with friends for the best co-op experience. Steam remote play or other third party screensharing apps could function as an alternative. Enter online at your own risk!

[h2]How does the playtest work?[/h2]

Pay a visit to our Store Page and request access to the Steam Playtest! This playtest will run from today, Friday 1/27 to Monday 1/30 and everyone who requests access will be permitted to play.

On Monday morning, we’ll close access in order to take some time digesting your feedback, incorporate it back into the game, and get ready for another playtest! 

You don’t even need to own the base game in order to access the playtest so if you don’t own the game, you can hop on in without spending a dime!


[h2]What is the purpose of this playtest?[/h2]

The purpose of this playtest is to gather feedback in order to improve and build out this new mode of play. As lots of its elements are experimental in nature, we wanted to hear what you’d like to see in a procedural escape room experience. Our hope is that by opening this up publicly, we can gather large amounts of player feedback and refine the update before its full release across all platforms.

We want to emphasize that this content is still in active development, and therefore players may experience issues that haven't been ironed out yet. So, while not the primary purpose of this playtest, we will also be making note of any major bugs discovered by players (and we appreciate the flagging of those when they occur).

Rigorous playtesting has always been a part of building [i]Escape Academy[/i], and Steam Playtests are a great chance to bring that to a significantly larger stage.


[h2]I’ve downloaded the build, how do I access Tournament of Puzzles?[/h2]

Once in build, start a new save and quickly play through the tutorial level and make your way to the map screen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/79da7d5232445fad574277e901904f1874194ee5.png[/img]

Once you arrive at the campus map, press TAB. Then, on the DLC select screen, select [i]Tournament of Puzzles.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/8116de96ef86c93af9dafc3afc5620d0b0714da4.png[/img]

After selecting [i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i] you will be placed into a 3D diorama. On the left is a TV screen labeled “Tournament Mode” that you can click to start your first heat in the tournament!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42120301/bb0af01d60ded3dcc188aa649e6c8474dae9e6e1.png[/img]

[h2]Where can we share our feedback?[/h2]

General feedback can be submitted on our Steam page or on the #feedback channel of our [url=https://discord.gg/P3RmrHtp]Discord[/url], but we’ve also built a questionnaire for more pointed questions and player input!

[url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdVguAqhkOlZA9et_HWNPlfruW16O94bHSi8H9RO2XJtBzeHw/viewform?usp=sf_link]Questionnaire Link[/url]

[h2]Will there be more playtests?[/h2]

Yes! Our goal is to run public playtests once a month until the full release of the [i]Tournament of Puzzles[/i] across all platforms.

[h2]Thanks for helping us make our game better![/h2]

As mentioned, playtesting is a critical piece of development at Coin Crew Games and we’re thrilled to bring more of our playerbase into the development of our content. 

Keep your eyes peeled on our [url=https://twitter.com/CoinCrewGames]Twitter[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/P3RmrHtp]Discord[/url], and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1812090/Escape_Academy/]Steam Page[/url] for future playtests and other [i]Escape Academy[/i] announcements!

Cheers, 
Coin Crew Games

notes.title: Escape from Anti-Escape Island - Upcoming Patch
notes.notes:
Hey there Escapists!

We've made it through launch weekend on our first DLC and are glad people have been able to experience what the Coin Crew Games team has been hard at work building the last few months. That being said, we've received reports of bugs and some feedback on the UX for specific puzzles and we wanted to let everyone know that we're aware and actively working on fixes! 

We are super appreciative of the feedback and we wanted to make sure the community knows we're taking the reports seriously and we're shooting to get a fix out as quickly as possible (while ensuring all the fixes are bulletproof).

[h2]What are we working on?[/h2]

There are a handful of nasty desync issues and one puzzle in particular has some UX smoothing out that's needed. More specific patch notes below.

[h3]POTENTIAL PUZZLE SPOILERS[/h3]

[list]
[*]Inappropriately large GPU consumption on Very High / Ultra graphics settings is getting smoothed out.
[*][spoiler]Chatterbox Achievement not firing properly on the base game after talking to the appropriate amount of characters is being fixed.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]On "The Experiment" there's multiple bugs with the spinning wheel, math puzzle on one of the turrets. These are being addressed.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]On "Into the Capture Dimension" there's issues where the laser-maze puzzle completes without placing the mirrors correctly and occasionally the mirrors get stacked on top of each other rendering the puzzle unsolvable. Both of these are being addressed.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Also on "Into the Capture Dimension," we've received a lot of feedback surrounding the UX on the mine field puzzle. In order to make this less frustrating, we are implementing a system that will reveal where previously triggered bombs are located on the board so it's not a COMPLETE reset every time a bomb is triggered.[/spoiler]
[/list]

If there are additional bugs that have effected your experience with the DLC, please let us know in the comments or on our Discord! We want to make sure this patch captures and fixes as many issues as time allows.

[h2]Timeline[/h2]

We are planning to push a new version of the game up to our "Hotfix" branch this Friday 11/18. 

As a heads up, it will take a bit longer to get the fixes pushed and ported to consoles, so for those cross-playing with friends on non-Steam platforms, there may be some compatibility issues on the hotfix branch as we're introducing new features for one of the puzzles.

Provided everything is stable, we'll get this all merged on to the main branch and all other platforms as soon as possible. 

[h2]A Note from Coin Crew Games[/h2]

For those of you who've had their experience with the DLC and Escape Academy soured by bugs, we are sorry! We hope that these fixes will encourage those who were unable to finish the DLC, to do so. 

Your feedback and engagement is important to us so PLEASE continue to flag things as they arise. We'll do our best to fix in a timely manner and take all of these learnings into future Escape Academy content.

Cheers, 
Coin Crew Games
